headline: Nvidia tells manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new US chip-license rule

facts.text: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
The pause is for an unspecified period while Nvidia assesses whether its regional partners are meeting US export requirements.
Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers in the four countries, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed earlier this month.
The US Commerce Department reportedly closed the remote-access loophole grudgingly.
The Institute for Progress, a think tank, estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China's AI computing power, according to the Journal.
The shipping halt follows a new US rule that would require licenses for companies in the four countries to buy advanced AI chips.
Bloomberg reports that Singapore is in talks with the US to retain access to advanced semiconductors, according to Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.

context: Nvidia designs the advanced AI chips, known as GPUs, that power large data centers. Server makers such as Dell and Super Micro build complete servers using those chips and sell them to customers. US export rules control which countries and companies can receive such advanced chips, and the Commerce Department enforces them.
why_it_matters: The pause and the new licensing rule affect companies and data center operators in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that need advanced AI chips. The reports also link the restrictions to limiting Chinese access to AI computing through remote data centers in the region.
open_questions: How long the shipment pause will last is not specified.
Whether Singapore will retain access to advanced chips after talks with the US is not yet known.
Whether Nvidia's regional partners are meeting US export requirements has not been determined.

headline: Anthropic goes public, trading as ANT

facts.text: Anthropic went public on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, valuing the company at approximately $1.5 trillion.
Anthropic's IPO was reportedly oversubscribed, with demand for six to seven times the number of available shares.
Anthropic generated $33 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, while reporting $104 billion in losses over the same period.
Anthropic has years of cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations reportedly amounting to around $518 billion.
Anthropic's IPO was reported as $81.3 billion in size, described by one outlet as a record for the largest IPO ever.
Anthropic shares fell below the $83 IPO price by November 24 and closed at $82.80 on November 25, according to Korea Daily.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei posted on X on November 25 that the claim he believes humans must hand over free will to AI is absurd.
The statement responded to an Axios report that a widespread view inside Anthropic holds humanity should hand over some decision-making power to superintelligent AI systems.
About 100 protesters gathered outside Anthropic's San Francisco headquarters on November 19 demanding a ban on Recursive Self-Improvement.

context: Anthropic is an AI company founded in 2021 that makes the Claude chatbot. An initial public offering (IPO) is when a private company first sells shares to the public on a stock exchange, after which its shares trade under a ticker symbol such as ANT.
why_it_matters: Anthropic is described as the first major stand-alone frontier AI lab to go public, so its share price and valuation are being watched by investors across the AI sector. Other AI-adjacent and cybersecurity stocks were reported rising as Anthropic began trading.
open_questions: Whether Anthropic's shares will hold above the $83 IPO price over time.

headline: Leading AI labs reportedly hold unreleased algorithmic breakthroughs that could threaten encryption; BoE's Bailey raises concern

facts.text: Scott Aaronson says he is virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that AI labs are sitting on one or more bombshells that could break deployed cryptosystems.
Aaronson says he feels much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells until he sees details or hears directly from someone at a lab.
Aaronson reports that OpenAI claims to prove that the matrix multiplication exponent omega is exactly 9/4.
Aaronson reports that OpenAI released a proof that the number of linear gates needed to compute the Fourier Transform is N (log N)^(1/2+o(1)).
Aaronson describes OpenAI's and Anthropic's proofs of VP ≠ VNP as recent results he was still processing.
Aaronson writes that he now feels for the first time that a proof of P ≠ NP is not far.
Axios reports, based on more than 20 interviews, that OpenAI and Anthropic staff fear new internal AI models are becoming too powerful to use safely.
According to Axios, researchers and executives at the two labs are split over how fast AI should develop and whether humans can guarantee control over powerful models.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said rapid development and safety do not necessarily conflict and that Anthropic would not speed up training and deployment until it had enough confidence in safety.
US President Donald Trump called calls for an AI slowdown a “hoax” that he said would weaken the United States against China.
The Financial Times reports that Andrew Bailey, Bank of England governor, says unreleased AI models have raised encryption concerns.
The Financial Times reports that breakthroughs in mathematics have stoked fears that data across financial systems is under threat.

context: Encryption protects data such as bank transfers and digital wallets using mathematical problems that are believed to be very hard to solve, so attacks on them typically require a major algorithmic advance. Matrix multiplication exponent and related complexity results are abstract measures of how efficiently computers can perform core calculations, studied in theoretical computer science. The Bank of England is the UK's central bank and regulator of financial stability.
why_it_matters: If AI-driven mathematical advances lead to algorithms that break currently deployed cryptosystems, data protected by those systems across financial and other sectors could be exposed. The concern is raised in the sources as a possibility; no break of deployed encryption is confirmed in them.

headline: Z.ai's GLM-5.5 delayed as US chip curbs and distillation crackdown slow Chinese AI models

Zhipu originally planned to release GLM-5.5 within the year, but the launch could slip until after the first quarter of next year.
Moonshot AI internally projects that losing overseas data center access could double its release interval from six months to over a year.
One source said Moonshot AI's flagship model Kimi K4 could be delayed until around mid-next year.
The U.S. Department of Commerce announced on November 16 a rule blocking Chinese companies from remotely renting Nvidia advanced chips through overseas data centers, effective November 19.
Overseas data centers providing a certain scale of computing to China must obtain a U.S. government license, with existing operators given a 90-day grace period.
Moonshot AI has reportedly canceled a $150 million Blackwell chip access contract through an Indonesian data center.
A source reported that inside DeepSeek, distillation being completely blocked could widen the gap with top U.S. models from 3 to 6 months to 9 months.
A researcher at a major Chinese tech company said "We are finished" and that many peers want to leave AI training work.
Anthropic and OpenAI have cracked down more aggressively on distillation since September, according to The Information.
The Japan Times reports that Z.AI has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship model, citing people familiar with the matter.

context: Z.ai (Zhipu) and Moonshot AI are Chinese companies developing large AI models. Distillation is a training method where a new model learns from the outputs of another model. Blackwell is Nvidia's latest advanced AI chip generation.
why_it_matters: The reported delays suggest U.S. chip access limits and anti-distillation measures could slow Chinese AI model development and widen the gap with top U.S. models, affecting Chinese AI developers and their cost advantage.
open_questions: Whether GLM-5.5 will be released in Q1 2027 or later remains unconfirmed.
How long the 90-day grace period for existing overseas data center operators will affect access.

headline: US approves Musk's plan for one million Starmind AI data-center satellites

facts.text: US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space.
The Federal Communications Commission said the project, known as Starmind, would support America's booming super intelligence economy.
The company wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send results back to Earth.
Under the FCC licence, deployment must begin no later than November 2033, with 10% deployed by November 2035 and 50% by November 2038.
SpaceX has said it wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year.
It is unclear whether a million satellites will indeed be launched or whether SpaceX sought approval for a higher number than it will use.
SpaceX believes orbital data centres are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet growing demand for AI computing power.
Rival firm Amazon criticised the plan as a lofty ambition rather than a real plan.
The American Astronomical Society said it was disheartened and dismayed by the decision and that the constellation would significantly undermine astronomical facilities and night-sky observation.
Musk responded on X saying the project will be a great asset to America and the world.
The Guardian reports that the Trump administration approved Musk's plan to create datacentres in space, with supporters arguing it will be more energy-efficient.

context: SpaceX is a rocket and satellite company owned by Elon Musk. Its Starlink network already provides high-speed internet through more than 10,000 satellites in low-Earth orbit. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is the US agency that licenses satellite launches and communications.
why_it_matters: The approval is the first of its kind for orbital data centres, a concept pitched as a less energy- and water-intensive alternative to ground-based data centres. Astronomers and the public who study or enjoy the night sky could be affected by the brighter, more numerous satellites.
open_questions: Whether a million satellites will actually be launched or whether the approved number exceeds what SpaceX will use.
Whether laser links from the ground can handle the large data volumes, according to Prof Sir Martin Sweeting.
Whether orbital data centres make sense at scale.

The raise is reportedly planned to start in the first quarter of 2027, though some investors want it to happen sooner.
The proposed $33 billion valuation would be 50% above the $22 billion valuation set in a $300 million employee tender offer in September.
ElevenLabs was last valued at $22 billion in September, in a $300 million employee tender offer led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price.
According to one person cited by Bloomberg, annualised revenue has reached about $700 million, up $100 million since September.
ElevenLabs declined to comment on the report.
In September, ElevenLabs said enterprise customers accounted for 55% of its revenue.
ElevenLabs agreed to acquire Japanese voice AI company Kotoba, with the deal expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.
CEO Mati Staniszewski has said the company could begin preparing for an IPO in 2028.

context: ElevenLabs is a London-based company that develops AI voice and audio models, including text-to-speech tools and conversational AI agents used in gaming, audiobooks and customer service. A Series D is a later-stage private funding round.
why_it_matters: The reported valuation would make ElevenLabs much more valuable within about 14 months, signalling strong investor appetite for AI voice technology. Its employees and existing shareholders could benefit if the round proceeds.

Whether the round will include a secondary sale for existing shareholders is not confirmed.

headline: Meta's Muse agent draws UK FCA complaint as AI shopping bots get Black Friday test

facts.text: Meta launched its Muse AI assistant in the UK this week, partnering with retailers including Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury's, JD Sports and Currys.
Meta says Muse can handle tasks such as Christmas shopping, searching for a cheaper energy deal and sorting the school calendar.
The UK Financial Conduct Authority complained that Meta declined its suggestion to jointly test Muse using the regulator's sandbox.
FCA head of innovation Colin Payne said the regulator wants to see what AI agents will do in the market, and that it is concerned about how payments are made by agents.
Payne said Meta only made the FCA aware of its Muse plans last month, leaving little time for testing.
Meta spokesperson Matthew Pollard said the company has engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities.
Meta says Muse must get the user's approval before making a purchase or sending an email in the UK, and Meta says it has no visibility into people's passwords or payment methods.
The UK Competition and Markets Authority has said it will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers if it has concerns about Muse.
According to YouGov, a third of people planning to shop during Black Friday intend to get help from AI this year, up from 19% last year.
Amazon has blocked AI agents from its store, though it is reportedly in talks with Meta about allowing Muse access.

context: Muse is Meta's AI assistant, marketed as a personal assistant that can carry out tasks like shopping on a user's behalf, and it is owned by the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. The Financial Conduct Authority is the UK financial regulator, and it runs a sandbox where firms can test new products under supervision. AI shopping agents are tools that make purchases or recommendations for users, which raises questions about payments, consumer protection and data use.
why_it_matters: UK shoppers and the retailers partnering with Meta are affected, since agents could change how purchases are made and how retailers reach customers. Regulators say they will monitor the rollout closely because many Britons already use Meta's products.
open_questions: Whether Meta will take part in joint testing with the FCA is not yet known.
How payments made by AI agents will work and be regulated is still unclear to the FCA.
Whether Amazon will allow Muse access to its store remains unresolved in the reports.

headline: Hochul vetoes AI safety bill; California governor presses AI bills; NY AG creates RAISE Act unit

facts.text: California Governor Gavin Newsom said his administration has drafted legislation to expand the state's AI safety protections and wants lawmakers to pass it within 30 days.
The recommendations would give California authority to order an emergency shutdown when an AI system poses an imminent danger and its developer cannot or will not contain it.
The governor's office calls the authority a "kill switch."
The state could also cap the computing capacity developers devote to automated AI research if the work outpaced safeguards and created a material risk of catastrophic harm.
Newsom said the governor would welcome a special session but needed legislative partners willing to act, and he had not yet called one.
Newsom predicted incoming Governor-elect Xavier Becerra would eventually enact the measures but estimated waiting would delay legislation by five or six months.
Becerra has endorsed expanded incident reporting and shutdown authority and said he would work quickly with lawmakers to put both into law.
The recommendations came from a Sept. 18 executive order by Newsom and an 85-page Government Operations Agency report issued Nov. 16.
The report identifies four levels of intervention: restricting access, stopping individual AI agents, isolating computing resources and suspending model operations.
OpenAI's chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane supported access for independent assessors and shutdown controls when lesser interventions would not contain a danger.

context: Gavin Newsom is California's governor, and the state has an existing AI law that defines catastrophic AI risk, including incidents causing more than 50 deaths or serious injuries or over $1 billion in damage. Recursive self-improvement refers to AI helping develop more capable AI. Governor-elect Xavier Becerra takes office in January and previously served as California attorney general.
why_it_matters: The proposals would give California emergency power to shut down or restrict dangerous AI systems and limit automated AI research, affecting AI developers such as OpenAI operating in the state. Newsom's timing depends on whether the outgoing legislature acts before Becerra takes office.
open_questions: Whether lawmakers will pass the legislation within 30 days or whether a special session will be called.
Whether Becerra and legislative leaders will adopt the measures on the timeline Newsom wants.
Whether the state will enact the shutdown and computing-cap authorities as recommended.

headline: 42 state AGs seek to block Character.AI from selling user chats in bankruptcy

facts.text: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling user data during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
The attorneys general accuse Character.AI of planning to auction off private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts.
The attorneys general say more than 2.1 million of the accounts are registered to minors.
The attorneys general say the sale offers no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold.
The attorneys general say the sale includes no requirement that the buyer honor existing privacy policies.
The attorneys general say users would have no avenue to delete their data and no inherent limit on what a buyer could do with it.
The attorneys general say the first bidder has a limited paper trail, having been established on November 13, 2026, with no parent company or investors listed.
Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October following years of scandals and legal challenges, including from Disney.
Disney bought some of Character.AI's assets and hired its CEO, Karandeep Anand, in an acquihire arrangement.
A broad coalition of attorneys general also opposed the Disney deal.
New York, Connecticut, California and Colorado have passed chatbot laws that Character.AI may be violating when they take effect on January 1, 2027.

context: Character.AI is a company that operates chatbots letting users hold conversations with AI characters. Chapter 11 is a U.S. bankruptcy process in which a company restructures or sells assets under court supervision, and in which assets such as customer data may be sold to creditors or buyers. Attorneys general are state officials who enforce consumer protection and privacy laws.
why_it_matters: The dispute concerns the private chat histories of millions of U.S. accounts, including more than 2.1 million accounts registered to minors, which could be sold to an unknown buyer. Users whose conversations are in the data would be directly affected.
open_questions: Whether the bankruptcy court will allow the sale of user chat data.
Who the first bidder for the chat data is, given its limited paper trail.
Whether Character.AI is in violation of the chatbot laws taking effect January 1, 2027.

headline: UN calls for global framework to govern AI risks within a year

facts.text: UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged member states to coordinate efforts to establish a comprehensive global framework for managing AI risks within the next year.
Guterres spoke on Monday at the Bridgetown AI Safety Summit in Barbados.
Guterres called for a globally inclusive, multilateral framework based on shared principles and supported by independent and credible oversight.
Guterres proposed starting with common AI safety measures, systems for testing AI technologies, and minimum requirements for independent supervision.
Guterres warned of future dangers from insufficient regulation, including the development of autonomous weapons systems.
Guterres called for reforms to international governance institutions, arguing many still reflect the global realities of 1945.
Guterres said effective AI oversight is one of the key recommendations he intends to pass on to his successor as his tenure ends.
The Finnish ministry of transport and communication said the summit's main message was that AI should be developed in a human-centric and well-governed manner.
The Finnish ministry said the 23 November UN Special Summit on AI Safety in Bridgetown, Barbados, also stressed more evenly shared AI benefits.

entities: Finnish ministry of transport and communication
context: The United Nations is the intergovernmental body whose Secretary-General, António Guterres, speaks on its behalf. Frontier AI models are the most advanced and capable AI systems, and governing them is a growing concern for governments. The UN Secretary-General's term is ending, so his recommendations are often passed to a successor.
why_it_matters: A call for a global AI risk framework signals that international leaders want coordinated oversight of AI, affecting governments and the AI developers they would regulate. The sources frame it as an effort to keep AI under human control amid intensifying competition between the United States and China.
open_questions: Which member states will commit to establishing the proposed global framework?
What specific form the independent oversight and minimum requirements would take is not yet detailed.

headline: Avicena raises $100M+ Series C for microLED chip interconnects

facts.text: Avicena, a Sunnyvale startup, has raised more than $100M in Series C funding.
InterVest led the round, Avicena announced on Tuesday.
Other investors include Tiger Global, Cerberus Capital Management, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund and AMD Ventures.
Kevin Pope succeeds Marco Chisari as chief executive of Avicena.
Avicena says its LightBundle platform uses dense arrays of microLEDs and silicon photodetectors linked by multicore fibre instead of lasers.
Avicena says copper links face limits on reach, density and energy use.
SK hynix has said the memory shortage will last until 2030.
Avicena began shipping 1Tbps LightBundle evaluation kits in August.
Pope said the new funding will go on hiring, product development and engineering.

Data centers have asked for about 34 GW of grid capacity in Norway, well above national peak demand of about 25 GW.
Only 0.8 GW of data center capacity is connected to the grid in Norway today.
Statnett has stopped granting new reservations and approving facility functionality while it sets functional requirements for data centers.
Projects with reserved capacity keep their place but still need approval before connecting, and existing connections are not affected.
Under the licensing scheme, new crypto sites will not be permitted and existing ones cannot get more grid capacity.
Under normal hydrology, Norway's net exports could fall 71%, from 14.3 TWh in 2027 to 4.1 TWh in 2030, according to Rystad's analysis.

context: Statnett is Norway's transmission system operator, responsible for the high-voltage grid that moves electricity across the country. Grid connection reservations are places in the queue that reserve future capacity for a facility. Norway has long had a power surplus, mostly from hydroelectric generation.
why_it_matters: The pause limits how fast data centers can connect, giving grid operator Statnett more control over incoming demand. Rystad's analysis suggests rising demand could erode Norway's power surplus and export advantage, which has kept its electricity prices low, affecting households and industry.
open_questions: What the functional requirements for data centers will specifically contain is not yet set.
Whether grid build-out will be ready in time for the queued projects' 2027-28 dates is unclear.
What gas with carbon capture and storage and offshore wind capacity the government wants data centers to help build is not yet decided.

facts.text: Houston-based geothermal startup Quaise Energy announced that Google agreed to buy 50 megawatts of carbon-free power from its first commercial project, Project Obsidian, near the Newberry Volcano in central Oregon.
Google said it plans to use the energy to help run its existing data center operations in northwest Oregon as early as 2030.

Quaise uses drilling techniques and rock-melting technology to access hotter geothermal resources than traditional plants can.
Quaise CEO Carlos Araque said the agreement marks a critical next step for Quaise and the clean energy sector.
Quaise said its Oregon project will cost about $350 million to build.
Quaise raised $180 million in equity financing in August, including investment from oil-and-gas drilling firm Nabors Industries.
Quaise is still testing the unique technology it plans to deploy for the Google-backed plant, and is working to drill over 3,200 feet at its Texas field site.

context: Geothermal power uses heat from beneath the Earth's surface to generate electricity. Conventional plants rely on naturally hot, permeable rock, while enhanced geothermal systems fracture rock and pump water through it to create artificial reservoirs. Superhot geothermal aims to reach rock above about 572 degrees Fahrenheit, which could yield more energy from fewer wells.
why_it_matters: The deal gives an advanced geothermal startup a major first customer, a step needed to raise financing for first-of-a-kind facilities. It also shows tech companies like Google seeking clean, around-the-clock power for their expanding data centers.

Who will buy the additional 200 MW of planned capacity at the Oregon site.
Whether the drilling technology will be deployed at commercial scale, as the technologies have not yet been widely deployed.

headline: India urges states to sign 41 GW of pending clean power contracts

facts.text: India's federal government urged states on Friday to sign more contracts for 41 gigawatts of clean energy capacity that has no buyers.
Shripad Naik, union minister of state for power and new and renewable energy, said states must identify power requirements well in advance.
Naik made the remarks at the State Power Ministers Conference in New Delhi.
The lack of battery energy storage left states scrambling for power to meet evening and night demand as El Nino pushed up consumption this year.
Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said an unexpected demand surge strained India's power system in September and October despite surplus solar energy.
Peak power demand of 271 GW in May was 11.6% higher than a year earlier, according to Agarwal.
Agarwal said there were days when India could barely meet evening peak demand despite surplus clean energy during the day.
Naik urged states to speed up payments tied to land acquisition for transmission projects, saying slow payments have caused huge delays.
Insufficient transmission capacity has forced India to curtail renewable power generation, wasting clean energy.

context: India's power system is run through a mix of central government ministries and individual state utilities, which buy electricity under long-term contracts with generators. Clean energy such as solar is cheap during the day but unavailable at night, so battery energy storage is used to hold power for evening and night demand. Transmission lines carry electricity from generation sites to consumers.
why_it_matters: States that fail to sign contracts leave clean energy capacity without buyers, and shortages of storage and transmission can leave evening demand unmet even when surplus solar exists. The national government is pushing states to plan ahead and sign contracts sooner.
open_questions: The sources do not say which states have yet to sign the pending contracts.
The sources do not give a timeline for when the 41 GW of contracts should be signed.

headline: Vietnam weighs delaying nuclear plants beyond 2035

facts.text: Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade has proposed a 2037 or 2038 start date for the Ninh Thuan 1 nuclear plant.
The Ministry proposes 2039 or 2040 as the start date for the Ninh Thuan 2 nuclear plant.
The proposal is part of a draft revision to the nation's power development plan, published for consultation.
The existing plan called for the Ninh Thuan 1 plant to become operational between 2030 and 2035.
Planners, including Russian partner Rosatom, assess that setting up the project takes a minimum of 12 years after a feasibility study is completed.
Vietnam Electricity Group (EVN) still proposes an earlier completion of 2034 or 2035 for Ninh Thuan 1 if conditions are favourable.
The revised plan also delays liquefied natural gas projects, with LNG-fired capacity expected to reach about 4.3 gigawatts by 2030, less than half the existing plan.
The revised plan scraps about six gigawatts of offshore wind capacity by 2030, while solar capacity is expected to rise to about 81.6 GW.
The Ministry of Industry and Trade has not said when it will make a final decision.
The Ministry presented nine scenarios and proposed scenario KB2A as the main option, according to a report on the second round of proposed adjustments to the Power Development Plan VIII.
Under scenario KB2A, nuclear capacity is projected at about 30,771 MW by 2050, with capital requirements for 2026-2050 estimated at around $187.3 billion.

context: Ninh Thuan is a site in south-central Vietnam where the country has long planned its first nuclear power plants. Vietnam Electricity Group (EVN) is the state-owned utility investing in Ninh Thuan 1, while Petrovietnam is the national oil and gas group developing Ninh Thuan 2. Power development plans are the government's long-term roadmaps for which generation sources will be built and when.
why_it_matters: The delays push back Vietnam's plan to use nuclear power to reduce its reliance on imported fossil fuels, a vulnerability the sources say was highlighted by soaring energy prices caused by the Iran war. The revised plan also affects gas and wind projects, shifting the country's power mix toward solar.
open_questions: When the Ministry of Industry and Trade will make a final decision on the revised plan is not yet known.
Whether EVN's earlier 2034-2035 timeline for Ninh Thuan 1 will be met depends on favourable mechanisms and policies not yet in place.

headline: Trump EPA keeps trying to kill Solar for All despite court losses

facts.text: The Trump administration appealed a court ruling that sought to restore the low-income Solar for All program.
Solar for All was first envisioned in 2022 as part of the Inflation Reduction Act.
In 2024 the EPA picked winners who would split a $7 billion pot to expand solar access for low-income and disadvantaged households.
In August 2025 the EPA announced it was killing Solar for All.
In September a federal judge ruled the EPA's rollback was illegal and that its reasoning for terminating the program was unjustified.
A second judge later ruled in favor of protecting Solar for All.
The EPA has never resumed grant handouts under the program.
Natural Resources Defense Council senior director Adam Kent said the administration is continuing its obstruction and delay.
Six Republican members of Congress wrote to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin urging the agency to swiftly reinstate the program.

context: Solar for All is a low-income solar program created under the Inflation Reduction Act, funding community solar, rooftop solar and battery storage through states, local governments, tribes and nonprofits. The EPA oversees the program and its grant awards. Its termination has been challenged in court by advocates, installers and a labor group.
why_it_matters: The fight determines whether low-income and disadvantaged households get access to cheaper solar power and battery storage that advocates say could lower energy bills. Grant recipients and communities planning these projects are directly affected by the delay.
open_questions: Whether the appeals court will overturn the ruling restoring the program.
Whether the EPA will reinstate grant payments.
How the remaining lawsuits seeking to recoup individual grants will be resolved.

headline: Compass may pause $380m ABS deal after investor rout following outage

facts.text: Compass Datacenters is reportedly pausing a $380 million asset-backed securities transaction following an investor rout after a data center outage.
Bloomberg reports that Compass no longer plans to complete the transaction this year and will put it off until next year.
The Bloomberg report relies on anonymous sources and had not been confirmed by Compass at the time of publication.
Compass has secured hundreds of millions of dollars in ABS deals this year and last year, including a $413 million transaction in July 2026.
The report links the deal delay to a data center outage, since an outage could threaten the revenue streams backing the bonds.
In April this year, Compass pulled out of the PW Digital Gateway project after legal challenges blocked its development.
Compass has around 16 data center sites in operation or under development across the US, Europe, and Israel.

context: Compass Datacenters is a data center developer founded in 2011. Asset-backed securities (ABS) are financial investments backed by a pool of assets; here, Compass typically uses its data centers as collateral, and bondholders are paid from tenant lease cash flows. Continuous uptime is the core product of a data center, so outages can affect those cash flows.
why_it_matters: A delay in the $380 million ABS transaction could affect Compass's ability to raise financing against its data center portfolio and signals investor concern after the outage. Compass's owners, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, are the companies that acquired it in 2023 for $5.5 billion.
open_questions: Compass has not yet confirmed the reported pause or the delay to next year.
The source does not say what caused the outage or how long it lasted.
Whether the transaction will ultimately be completed in 2027 is not stated.

headline: Cheyenne Light seeks transmission for three Microsoft data centers in Wyoming

facts.text: Cheyenne Light, a Wyoming utility, has applied to FERC to build transmission and distribution infrastructure for three planned Microsoft data centers.
Microsoft will pay for the infrastructure through a contribution in aid of construction and an up-front payment.
The filed agreements are redacted, so their size and terms are not publicly available.

Cheyenne Light plans to serve the data centers under its large load tariff.

The utility filed the Microsoft agreements with FERC in a November 24, 2026 filing.
Two Bright Horizon transmission projects in Wyoming carry an estimated combined investment of $686 million, pending Wyoming Public Service Commission approval.

headline: Japan's METI awards Kyoto Fusioneering-led consortium up to JPY 23.3bn for tokamak demonstration

facts.text: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry formally confirmed a subsidy award of up to JPY 23.3 billion to a consortium led by Starlight Engine, a Kyoto Fusioneering group company.
The subsidy is for a fusion power generation demonstration project running from fiscal year 2026 through 2028.
The grant aims to demonstrate actual power generation from fusion using a tokamak device with high-temperature superconducting coils.
The formal selection was announced in November 2026, after a conditional selection announced on August 31, 2026.
The consortium will carry out design work and component technology development across 10 integrated engineering areas, according to the Fusion Industry Association.
The planned power generation demonstration is to take place at FAST, Starlight Engine's integrated tokamak demonstration plant, in the 2030s.
The goal of the three-year effort is to mature engineering technologies, not to build a complete power plant.
Kyoto Fusioneering named Pattrick Calderoni, formerly fusion program lead at Idaho National Laboratory, as Director of Blanket Programs, announced November 20, 2026.
Calderoni will serve as co-Chief Scientist for UNITY-3, a 14 MeV blanket test facility being developed by Kyoto Fusioneering with Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
UNITY-3 will expose blanket mock-ups to 14 MeV neutrons to provide measured data for checking blanket design simulation codes.

context: METI is Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, which funds strategic technologies through government budgets. Kyoto Fusioneering is a private company focused on commercializing fusion energy. A tokamak is a doughnut-shaped magnetic device that confines hot plasma to produce fusion; high-temperature superconducting coils generate strong magnetic fields more efficiently than older superconducting designs.
why_it_matters: The award puts public money behind a privately led effort to build the engineering foundations for fusion electricity, a technology that has not yet produced commercial power anywhere. Japan's government backing signals it sees this approach as credible for its energy security and decarbonization goals.
open_questions: Whether the FAST demonstration will actually produce fusion-generated electricity in the 2030s is not yet known.
The sources do not detail how the subsidy funds will be split among consortium members.

headline: Avantus signs PG&E PPAs for 800 MW solar and 3,200 MWh storage

facts.text: Avantus signed 20-year power purchase agreements with Pacific Gas and Electric for its Buttonbush 1A and 1B projects in Kern County, California.
Buttonbush 1A and 1B together add up to 800 MW of solar and 3,200 MWh of battery storage.
Avantus estimates the build will cost about $3 billion.

Avantus CEO Cliff Graham said Buttonbush would keep low-cost solar flowing into the evening, when demand peaks.
PG&E's Gillian Clegg said the projects will be among the largest clean energy resources in the utility's portfolio.
Avantus plans to keep ownership of Buttonbush 1A and 1B and operate both projects itself as an independent power producer.
The projects will be built on water-stressed farmland, which Avantus presents as a way to help meet the state's groundwater requirements.
Avantus estimates the projects will produce hundreds of millions of dollars in local property taxes over their operating life.

context: Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E) is a major California utility that buys electricity under long-term contracts to serve its customers. A power purchase agreement (PPA) is a long-term contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase electricity from a generator at set terms. Battery storage, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh), lets solar power be stored and released later, such as in the evening.

headline: Australia launches CIS tender for up to 5 GW of renewables

headline: Volvo Cars begins training Hexagon humanoid robots for Ghent factory work ahead of 2027 rollout

headline: Jensen Huang reportedly resigns as Nvidia CEO amid scandal, then is reinstated

facts.text: Jensen Huang announced his resignation as NVIDIA president and CEO on Thursday, November 12, 2026, amid affair concerns.

headline: US probes Waymo over school bus passing; recall covers 4,488 vehicles

context: Waymo is a self-driving robotaxi service owned by Alphabet. The sources say no collisions or injuries were reported in the closed-lane events.
open_questions: Whether the December 2025 software update fixed the school bus problem, which NHTSA will determine in its investigation.
What the final remedy for the closed-lane recall will be, since the filing said it was still under development.
Whether the school bus investigation will lead to a recall covering about 2,895 vehicles.

headline: Japan's Noetra launches with 44 companies for domestic physical AI, METI backing up to ¥1.3 trillion

facts.text: Noetra, a new company, began full operations in July to develop a Japanese-made AI foundation model meant to serve as the brain of robots.
SoftBank, Sony Group, Honda, NEC and 40 other Japanese companies have come together to form Noetra.
Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry has indicated it will provide support totaling at least ¥1.3 trillion, approximately $8.2 billion.
Under the fiscal 2026 budget, METI will spend roughly ¥390 billion to procure about 27,500 GPUs from Nvidia for developing foundation models.
The GPUs are planned for installation at a large data center in Sakai.
The ¥1.3 trillion support figure is based on the fiscal 2026 budget proposal, and some point to the risk that national spending will swell.
Hirotora Tamba, who became Noetra's president, met Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on the 12th and made the case for developing Japanese-made AI.
Daisuke Okanohara of Preferred Networks and Yoshihisa Ijiri of SoftBank's AI development subsidiary were appointed co-heads of development.
About 100 engineers have been dispatched by the participating companies to the core development work.
Japan fell behind the United States and China in language models and is seeking a comeback in physical AI, AI embodied in the physical world.
OpenAI and Anthropic are investing on a scale of tens of trillions of yen to ¥100 trillion, and China is also backing AI and humanoid robot development nationally.

context: METI, Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, is the government ministry that promotes industrial policy and funds technology development. A foundation model is a large AI model trained on broad data that can be adapted to many tasks, and physical AI refers to AI that controls or is embodied in robots and machines that act in the physical world.
why_it_matters: The effort is Japan's attempt to regain competitiveness in AI after falling behind the United States and China in language models, and it could shape domestic industries such as manufacturing. The large government spending means taxpayers and the participating companies are both affected by whether it pays off.
open_questions: Whether Japan can turn the 27,500 GPUs' computing infrastructure into development results efficiently.
Whether Japan can detach its physical AI foundation models from dependence on overseas technology.
Whether the total government support will grow beyond the ¥1.3 trillion figure based on the fiscal 2026 budget proposal.

headline: Uber begins driverless Lucid Gravity robotaxi tests in Bay Area

facts.text: Nuro, Lucid and Uber announced on November 24, 2026 that Lucid Gravity robotaxis entered driverless public-road testing in California.
The driverless testing takes place in Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale, California.
The new phase has no safety driver inside the vehicle, according to Nuro's announcement.
Uber Technologies has started fully driverless robotaxi testing in the San Francisco Bay Area with Lucid vehicles and Nuro technology.
Nuro says supervised public-road testing in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston began in December 2025.
Lucid has delivered more than 100 updated vehicles for the next phase of testing.
Nuro expects public robotaxi service in the Bay Area in Q1 2027, which is a target rather than a confirmed launch date.
Employee rides are the planned next step before public service.
Nuro supplies the Nuro Driver Level 4 autonomy platform, while Lucid supplies the modified Gravity vehicles and Uber provides its ride-hailing network.
Samarth Kejriwal, Uber's global head of autonomous mobility, said partners still need to refine operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience before driverless passenger rides.
NVIDIA DRIVE said its DRIVE AGX Thor platform powers Nuro Driver in this program.

context: Uber Technologies operates app-based platforms that match riders with drivers and connect users to delivery and freight services. Lucid makes the Gravity electric vehicle, and Nuro develops the autonomous driving software used in these test vehicles. A safety driver is a human who sits in the vehicle to take over if the autonomous system fails.
why_it_matters: The move from supervised to fully driverless testing on public roads is a step toward Uber offering robotaxi rides to the public. Riders and investors in Uber would be affected if the planned 2027 rollout proceeds on schedule.
open_questions: Whether public robotaxi service in the Bay Area will launch in Q1 2027 as targeted.
When employee rides will begin.
What operational, infrastructure and in-cabin experience refinements remain before driverless passenger rides.

headline: Robotera deploys 45 M7 humanoids at China Post's Hangzhou hub

facts.text: ROBOTERA says 45 of its humanoid robots have been deployed at China Post's Hangzhou Postal District Center.
The robots perform parcel induction tasks, including picking, reorienting, rejecting irregular parcels, and handling operational exceptions.
China Post's Hangzhou center began testing ROBOTERA's robots for parcel induction in April 2026.
ROBOTERA reports induction efficiency rose from 500–600 parcels per hour initially to about 1,200 per hour during specific testing periods.
ROBOTERA reports operational accuracy has exceeded 90%.
ROBOTERA calls this the largest deployment of robots for testing in comparable postal operations nationwide.
A separate report says the Hangzhou efficiency has since risen above 1,500 items per hour.
China Post's Hangzhou branch says it plans to expand automated equipment, including intelligent sorting and security inspection systems, to more operations.
Gasgoo reports that ROBOTERA's robots already operate across eleven postal nodes in eight cities in Guangdong.

entities: China Post Hangzhou Postal District Center
context: ROBOTERA is a robotics company that develops general-purpose humanoid robots. Parcel induction is the step in a sorting operation where packages are placed onto platforms that feed them into the sorting system. China Post is China's national postal operator.
why_it_matters: The deployment is described as one of the largest robot trials in Chinese postal operations, relevant to postal workers and logistics operators considering automation. The sources present the performance figures as company-reported test results.
open_questions: The sources do not say whether the robots will move beyond testing to permanent operation.
The sources give different efficiency figures (1,200 and above 1,500 per hour) and do not explain the measurement basis for each.
It is not stated how the robots' performance compares with human workers at the Hangzhou facility.

headline: EU delays vote on Tesla self-driving to December 15

facts.text: The European Union has postponed its meeting to vote on bloc-wide approval of Tesla Assisted Driving from Dec. 1 to Dec. 15, according to Reuters.
The EU vote was initially expected to conclude in October, so this is another delay.
Tesla has secured national approval for its system in 12 EU countries, with Italy the latest to authorize it.
EU-wide approval requires support from at least 15 of the bloc's 27 member states, representing 65% of its population.
The Dutch regulator RDW granted the first national approval on April 10.
Tesla renamed its system in Europe from Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to Tesla Assisted Driving, clarifying that it assists drivers rather than offering full autonomy.
Tesla reduced the maximum speed offset from 50% to 10% above the posted limit, and the setting resets to zero at each vehicle start.
Germany is an important prospect for approval after pushing Tesla to address concerns about the system's capabilities and safety.
No reason has been given for the delay, according to GuruFocus.
Elon Musk said on the third-quarter call that he would be surprised if approval took longer than the first quarter of 2027.
A rejection at the EU level would invalidate national approvals already granted, potentially leaving customers in the 12 approved countries unable to use the system.

context: Tesla Assisted Driving is Tesla's driver-assistance software, formerly sold in Europe as Full Self-Driving (Supervised). It requires the driver to stay attentive and responsible. In the EU, national regulators can approve a system on their own, but an EU-wide approval requires a vote by member state representatives on a technical committee.
why_it_matters: Tesla needs EU-wide approval to expand the system beyond the 12 countries that have approved it, which matters for its European business and its push to grow software subscription revenue. Customers in approved countries could also be affected if the EU rejects the system.
open_questions: Whether the EU committee will approve Tesla Assisted Driving on December 15.
Whether Germany and other large economies will support approval.
The reason for the repeated delays, which no source has explained.

headline: Rockwell Automation to acquire AGILOX

facts.text: Rockwell Automation has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Austria-based AGILOX, a maker of AMRs.
AGILOX's AMRs are driven by self-developed AI and swarm networking technology.
Terms of the acquisition, including the price, were not disclosed.
Rockwell said AGILOX's forklift AMR portfolio and OTTO's flatbed AMR platform will together create a comprehensive autonomous material movement system.
Rockwell said the acquisition will combine OTTO's strong presence in North America with AGILOX's established footprint across Europe.
Rockwell said the acquisition will more than double its AMR business.
Rockwell CEO Blake Moret said combining AGILOX and OTTO technologies creates a best-in-class technology platform.
AGILOX co-CEOs said joining Rockwell gives AGILOX the scale and market reach they could not build on their own.
The transaction is subject to closing conditions and regulatory approval, and Rockwell expects it to close in the second quarter of its fiscal year 2027.

context: AGILOX is an Austria-based maker of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), which are driverless vehicles that move materials around factories and warehouses. Rockwell Automation is a US industrial automation company that already owns OTTO, a maker of flatbed AMRs. Material movement refers to transporting goods across a plant floor or warehouse.
why_it_matters: The deal combines Rockwell's North American AMR presence with AGILOX's European footprint, expanding Rockwell's autonomous material handling offering for manufacturers and warehouse operators. Rockwell says it will more than double its AMR business.
open_questions: The purchase price was not disclosed.
Whether regulatory approval will be granted is not yet known.
The deal is expected to close in Rockwell's fiscal Q2 2027, but the closing is subject to conditions.

headline: XPeng unveils Turing physical AI architecture alongside IRON humanoid

facts.text: XPeng unveiled its Turing Physical AI Architecture, also called VLA 3.0, at its eighth XPeng AI Day in Guangzhou.
The architecture is shared across XPeng's intelligent vehicles and humanoid robots.
XPeng's humanoid robot IRON made its first public debut.
The architecture connects three systems: System 0 (ultra-fast control), System 1 (fast perception and action, powered by VLA 2.0) and System 2 (slow task planning and reasoning).
IRON is scheduled to begin training as a store assistant in XPeng retail stores in Q1 2027, with its official public release targeted for Q2 2027.
In tests in urban congestion conditions, XPeng's VLA Adaptive Deceleration feature increased usable driving range by 12.4% compared with energy recovery switched off.
The VLA Adaptive Deceleration feature is scheduled for its first over-the-air rollout in December 2026.
XPeng CEO He Xiaopeng says humanoid robots need several speeds of thought and that hardware must come first.
According to He Xiaopeng's article in The Economist's The World Ahead 2027, 2027 is expected to mark the start of mass production of advanced general-purpose humanoid robots.
XPeng says its first purpose-built robotaxi model for commercial deployment, YOYO-01, is scheduled for release in 2027.

context: XPeng is a Chinese electric vehicle maker that describes itself as a physical AI company, applying AI to cars and humanoid robots. VLA stands for vision-language-action, a class of AI models that link perception and language to physical actions. A humanoid robot is a human-shaped robot designed for general-purpose tasks.
why_it_matters: The architecture aims to let one AI stack serve both XPeng's cars and its robots, which the company says can speed up development. For retail customers and workers, IRON's planned store role is an early test of humanoid robots in commercial settings.
open_questions: Whether IRON's store training and public release will happen on the announced schedule.
When the full adaptive deceleration and active avoidance features will be broadly available beyond the planned December 2026 rollout.

headline: Eric Trump-backed robot startup's staff lose health insurance as it seeks $150 million

facts.text: Employees of Foundation Future Industries, a humanoid robotics startup backed by Eric Trump, have lost employer-provided health benefits after weeks without pay.
Foundation told employees that benefits administered by Rippling ended retroactively to October, according to an internal memo CNBC reported citing.
Foundation blamed its benefits administrator, Rippling, saying the last pay run through Rippling was in October.
Foundation promised to reimburse workers for COBRA continuation coverage and find a replacement provider, but employees questioned whether it could afford those reimbursements.
Rippling disputed Foundation's account, telling CNBC that clients failing to meet payroll and benefits obligations over multiple months receive a warning before termination.
Employees last received paychecks on October 15, and some worry about another missed payday on November 30.
CNBC first reported the unpaid wages on November 14, alongside a $4.6 million company loan that co-founder and CEO Sankaet Pathak took in 2025.
Pathak told employees the loan arrangement had no relationship to the current cash situation, according to a Reuters report.
Foundation is pursuing a bridge loan ahead of a possible $150 million investment from South Korea's Base Group.
Reuters reported on November 19 that Base confirmed it was considering funding, but no deal was final.

context: Foundation Future Industries is a humanoid robotics startup. COBRA is a federal rule that generally lets workers who lose employer health coverage keep it temporarily, though they often must pay the full premium themselves. Rippling is an HR and payroll software provider that administered the company's benefits and payroll.
why_it_matters: Employees are losing health coverage and pay while the company seeks emergency financing, leaving some worried about affording rent and keeping family members' medical treatment covered. The outcome depends on whether the bridge loan and the possible Base Group investment close.
open_questions: Whether the bridge loan or the possible $150 million Base Group investment will be finalized.
Whether Foundation can afford the promised COBRA reimbursements.
Whether employees will be paid on the November 30 payday.

headline: Tesla releases FSD v15 with camera visuals, drops interventions menu

facts.text: Tesla removed the Interventions menu from Full Self-Driving in its v15 update.
The Interventions menu was introduced with FSD v14 and offered four options: Parking, Navigation, Critical, and Other.
The menu would not disappear until the driver selected one of its options, and many owners selected Critical every time.
FSD v15 rollout began for Early Access Program participants on a weekend before November 26, 2026.
Tesla expects the system to reduce critical interventions by 25 times, a projection the sources do not confirm as independently verified.
The v15 update adds avoidance of potholes and debris on the road, navigation improvements, and a new Reality View feature.
Tesla has not said why it removed the Interventions menu; reporting offers possible explanations but no confirmed reason.
Elon Musk posted "Teslas have superhuman vision" on X, quoting a user's clip of FSD V15 in heavy rain.
The rain clip is a single user's account; the source provides no independent measurements of detection accuracy.
Tesla shares rose 2.22% to $388.57 in overnight trading on Thursday, according to the report.
Tesla may begin trials of renting Model Y vehicles to the Tesla Robotaxi fleet next month, according to reports.

context: Full Self-Driving (FSD) is Tesla's driver-assistance software, which requires an attentive driver to supervise it at all times. Early Access Program participants are owners who test new versions before wider release. An intervention is when a driver takes manual control from the system.
why_it_matters: The change removes a prompt that many owners found annoying, which may make FSD easier to use day to day. Tesla's performance claims about the update, including the projected 25-fold drop in critical interventions, remain company claims without independent verification.
open_questions: Why Tesla removed the Interventions menu has not been confirmed.
Whether the projected 25-fold reduction in critical interventions holds up has not been independently verified.
Whether the rain visualization performs reliably in heavy weather is unknown beyond one user's clip.

headline: Boston Dynamics expands GlobalFoundries partnership with Spot and Atlas in semiconductor fabs

facts.text: Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries announced an expanded collaboration to deploy the Spot quadruped robot for autonomous enterprise asset management across GF's global semiconductor fabs.
Boston Dynamics said Spot deployments will expand to GF manufacturing sites in Malta, New York; Burlington, Vermont; Dresden, Germany; and Singapore.
Boston Dynamics said GlobalFoundries will be the first customer outside the automotive industry to begin testing the Atlas humanoid robot in its early adopter program.
Boston Dynamics said the Atlas program is the first of its kind for semiconductor manufacturing.
GlobalFoundries has deployed Spot at its Burlington, Vermont site for more than four years.

According to Boston Dynamics, two Spot robots in Singapore have traveled nearly 900 kilometers and completed more than 90,000 inspections in sub-fab areas since April, with a 99% mission success rate.
Boston Dynamics said GF redeployed 875 routine inspections in just two weeks and has a roadmap to more than double that number.
Pradip Singh, GlobalFoundries' chief manufacturing officer, said Spot has helped the company shift from reactive to predictive maintenance.
According to the companies, testing of Atlas on-site at GF facilities will begin in early 2027.
The companies said the Atlas skills development workshop aims to evaluate potential humanoid use cases and assess customer readiness and integration needs.
Zack Jackowski, Boston Dynamics' chief product and technology officer, said GlobalFoundries was one of the company's earliest Spot customers.

context: Boston Dynamics is a robotics company known for legged robots. Spot is a four-legged quadruped robot used for autonomous inspection and data collection. Atlas is the company's humanoid robot. GlobalFoundries is a semiconductor chip manufacturer with fabrication plants (fabs) around the world.
why_it_matters: The expansion shows robots being used for routine inspection and predictive maintenance in chip factories, which can reduce downtime. Testing a humanoid robot like Atlas in this setting is an early step toward robots doing more factory tasks.
open_questions: What specific tasks Atlas will be trained to perform remains to be determined through the testing workshop.
Whether the humanoid testing will lead to broader deployment is not stated.

headline: Artificial Analysis humanoid simulation test finds OpenAI ahead of Google and Anthropic

facts.text: Artificial Analysis released a humanoid robotics benchmark called AA-Robotics-Sim v0.1 on Nov. 25.
OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra outperformed rival models from Anthropic and Google in the benchmark, according to the report.
The benchmark evaluated nine language models controlling a simulated Unitree G1 humanoid robot with 29 joints and three-fingered hands.
Each AI model writes and executes code to direct the simulated robot, while a separate controller keeps it balanced.
Astra finished 13.5 points ahead of its closest competitor, with scores measured out of 100 including partial credit.
No model managed to get a single piece of laundry into the washing machine during the evaluation.
Across 90 dishwasher trials, the models placed only five dishes in the rack.
Researchers identified grasping as a persistent problem, with box-moving attempts pressing items between palms rather than closing fingers around them.
All nine models earned full marks in warehouse navigation, maneuvering around packages without moving them.
In a separate experiment with a dish told to be fragile, seven models broke it at least once, including Astra.

context: Humanoid robots are human-shaped machines with arms, hands and legs. Large language models (LLMs) are AI systems that can be used to write code, and in this benchmark they write the code that directs a simulated robot's movements. Benchmarks like this are standardized tests used to compare AI systems on the same tasks.
why_it_matters: The results suggest that current AI models can navigate spaces but struggle with the grasping and manipulation needed for household and industrial chores, which matters to companies developing or deploying robots.
open_questions: Whether the simulated results would hold on physical robots is not addressed in the source.
The source does not say how the models would perform on tasks beyond the 10 assignments tested.

headline: IFR: Robot density in manufacturing reaches a new peak

facts.text: The International Federation of Robotics (IFR) reports that global robot density in manufacturing has reached a new peak.
The IFR says the global average baseline for robot density has risen to 152 industrial robots per 10,000 employees.
South Korea remains the world's leader in robot density, with 1,066 industrial units per 10,000 employees.
Singapore ranks second with 873 units per 10,000 employees, and Germany ranks third with 469 units.
The IFR says robot density in the European Union rose about 35% from 2020 to 2025, reaching a record 240 units.
The IFR reports that North America's robot density rose about 24% from 2020 to 2025, reaching 214 units.
The United States ranks 8th worldwide with 323 units per 10,000 employees.
The IFR says Japan ranks 4th globally with 452 units per 10,000 employees.
The IFR says China, the world's largest market for industrial robots, has a robot density of 193 units, ranking 19th globally.
The IFR says China's robot density increased 147% from 2020 through 2025.

context: Robot density is the number of operational industrial robots per 10,000 employees in a given sector, used to compare automation levels across countries on an equal basis. The International Federation of Robotics is an industry organization that publishes robotics statistics, including this periodic robot density report.
why_it_matters: The figures show that industrial automation in manufacturing keeps rising worldwide, with the largest recent gains in Asia and China. They offer countries and manufacturers a benchmark for comparing how heavily their factories rely on robots.

headline: XPeng to trial humanoid as store assistant in Q1 2027; says household chore robots in 1-2 years

facts.text: XPeng unveiled its humanoid robot IRON in Guangzhou.
XPeng plans to train IRON as a store assistant in its retail outlets from January to March 2027.
According to CNBC, XPeng plans to start mass production of IRON in January 2027 and open sales in the second quarter.
XPeng says household chore robots could arrive within one to two years.
XPeng targets a public release of IRON between April and June 2027.
Co-President Brian Gu told CNBC that making a robot walk, answer questions and use its hands at once is the hardest challenge.
XPeng's robotics unit raised $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation this summer, in a round led by IDG Capital.
XPeng unveiled its Turing Physical AI Architecture, designed to connect AI decision-making with control of vehicle and robot movements.

context: XPeng is a Chinese electric vehicle maker that is expanding into humanoid robots and flying vehicles. A humanoid robot is a general-purpose robot built with a human-like body, designed to perform a range of tasks. Training a robot as a store assistant means teaching it to handle everyday customer interactions and tasks in a real retail setting before wider sales.
why_it_matters: The plan tests whether humanoid robots can handle real customer-facing work outside demos, which affects shoppers at XPeng showrooms and future home buyers. XPeng says home models depend on how well the store trials go.
open_questions: Whether IRON can handle everyday store questions and tasks reliably during the trials.
Whether home versions will arrive within the one to two years XPeng suggests.
Exact pricing and sales details beyond the planned timeline.

headline: Waymo struggles on freeways despite city success

facts.text: A driverless Waymo was filmed trying to pass two California Highway Patrol cruisers during a traffic break on Interstate 280 on November 6.
The California DMV last week banned Waymo vehicles from all state interstates.
Between October and November 2026, Waymo reported 11 cases in which its vehicles drove into freeway lanes closed for construction, according to a recently filed recall.
Waymo paused commercial freeway rides across all its U.S. markets last week.
Earlier this year Waymo temporarily halted freeway rides after its robotaxis entered active construction zones in Arizona and California, then issued a recall in June.
Waymo gradually resumed freeway operations in late July after updating its software.
Phil Koopman, a Carnegie Mellon University professor, says Waymo is using recalls as Band-Aids and that the recalls did not fix the problem.
Waymo said its vehicles had not crashed or injured anyone while driving through restricted freeway areas.
Waymo spokesperson Chris Pappas said the company is working with the California DMV to resume freeway operations.
Waymo's Dmitri Dolgov said in November 2025 that freeway driving is very easy to learn but very hard to master with full autonomy.

context: Waymo is a robotaxi company operating driverless ridehailing vehicles in several U.S. cities. The California DMV regulates autonomous vehicle testing and operation in the state. Recalls filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration are formal reports by manufacturers that announce software or other fixes for safety defects.
why_it_matters: The freeway pause and state ban limit Waymo's service and make trips longer for customers who rely on highways to reach destinations such as airports. The episodes also raise questions for regulators and the public about whether driverless vehicles are safe at highway speeds.
open_questions: When Waymo will resume freeway operations is not stated in the sources.
Whether the recalls have fixed the construction-zone problem is disputed by experts.
What the California DMV will require before lifting its ban is not stated in the sources.

headline: Figure AI answers Musk's 'staged demo' criticism with apple demo video

facts.text: Figure AI released a video on November 23 showing its Figure 03 humanoid robot picking up an apple, with the table then moved.
After the table was moved, the robot adjusted its movements and successfully picked up the apple again, according to the video's description.
Brett Adcock, Figure AI's founder and CEO, said the robot was never trained in this environment and moved fully autonomously.
The video was posted as a response to Elon Musk's claim that most humanoid robot demonstrations are staged or rely on pre-programming.
Musk made his criticism at the Tomorrow X Summit on November 18, using an apple-on-a-table scenario as an example.
Musk said Tesla's Optimus robot could show an authentic demonstration within a month or two.
Some users praised Figure's progress, while others questioned how many attempts the video took and whether the robot truly moved autonomously.
Some analysts say it is unclear whether Adcock reproduced the exact scenario Musk had in mind, since Musk did not say whether the robot was already moving when the table shifted.

context: Figure AI is a U.S. humanoid robot startup that builds general-purpose robots. Tesla CEO Elon Musk is developing his own humanoid robot, Optimus. Whether a robot is truly autonomous or relies on pre-programmed routines is a central debate in the field.
why_it_matters: The dispute bears on whether humanoid robots can perform tasks in unfamiliar conditions rather than only in rehearsed demonstrations. Viewers and investors weigh company claims about autonomy against the limits of a single video.
open_questions: How many attempts were needed to capture the video, which has not been reported.
Whether the robot would still succeed if the apple fell off the table or rolled away.
Whether Tesla will release the authentic Optimus demonstration Musk promised within a month or two.

headline: Tesla expands Dallas robotaxi area, with over 1,000 Cybercabs on Texas roster

facts.text: The Texas Department of Motor Vehicles listed 1,841 vehicles under Tesla Robotaxi LLC on November 26.
The FSD Database breakdown showed 1,107 Cybercabs and 734 Model Ys on Tesla's Texas roster.
Tesla added 285 Cybercabs compared with the previous check, which counted 822 Cybercabs.
The FSD Database reported that the latest batch consisted of 2027-model-year Cybercabs.
Cybercabs now make up about 60% of Tesla's Texas roster, up from about 53% in the previous check.
Tesla started carrying paying Cybercab passengers in Austin in September and brought the cars to Dallas in November.
The Texas roster counts vehicles under the operator's Texas authorization and does not show how many are picking up passengers.
According to the NextBigFuture blog, Tesla's Dallas robotaxi service area doubled to 150 square miles.

context: Cybercab is a two-seat Tesla vehicle built for driverless rides, with no steering wheel or pedals. Texas requires autonomous vehicle operators to list their vehicles with the state Department of Motor Vehicles, so the roster is a count of authorized vehicles rather than vehicles actively carrying riders.
why_it_matters: The growth in listed Cybercabs signals Tesla is scaling its driverless robotaxi service in Texas, which affects riders in Austin and Dallas and rival ride-hailing services.
open_questions: How many of the listed vehicles are actually picking up passengers is not stated.
The sources do not say which city will receive the next batch of Cybercabs.
The sources do not confirm the Dallas service area expansion beyond one blog's claim.

headline: NIO unveils NWM3.0 world model; Xiaomi adds on-vehicle world model

facts.text: NIO unveiled its self-developed NWM3.0 world model and the NOMI Intelligence 4.0 vehicle-wide intelligence architecture at its 2026 NIO Innovation Tech Day in Guangzhou on November 25.
NIO Chairman William Li said cumulative R&D investment exceeded 72 billion yuan, approximately $10.8 billion, through the first half of this year.
According to the Shanghai Securities News, NWM3.0 achieves data iteration efficiency up 3x and data scale expanded 7x.
NIO says NWM3.0's overall training efficiency is 5x that of conventional versions.
NIO says it reduced the on-device compute overhead of attention mechanisms through dual closed-loop training and other methods, and these figures are internal test results.
NIO defines NOMI Intelligence 4.0 as the industry's first vehicle-wide intelligence architecture truly driven by native agents.
Starting December 2026, after regulatory approval in China, NIO plans phased OTA updates to all NIO and ONVO models equipped with four intelligent systems: Banyan, Cedar, Cedar S and Coconut+.
NIO has not yet disclosed the hardware threshold for NWM3.0 or the scope of compatibility with older models.

context: NIO is a Chinese electric vehicle maker. A world model is an AI system that learns to represent and predict how the physical environment behaves, used in autonomous and assisted driving. Onboard compute refers to the processing chips inside the vehicle that run such models in real time.
why_it_matters: If NIO's compute and latency figures hold up on production vehicles, the technology could bring advanced driver-assistance features to NIO and ONVO owners in more price bands. Investors are watching whether the large R&D spending turns into sales and margin gains.
open_questions: What hardware is required to run NWM3.0?
Which older NIO models will be compatible?
Will the reported compute and latency gains be confirmed on large-scale production vehicles?

headline: Unitree's Wang Xingxing says China robot output will overtake cars in 5-10 years

facts.text: Wang Xingxing, founder and chairman of Unitree Robotics, made two judgments at the WISE2026 Business King Conference in Beijing on the 26th.
Wang estimated that within 5 to 10 years, China's annual robot output could catch up with or even exceed automobile production.
Wang said that if a promising technology direction emerges, Unitree's profit level 'may decline slightly'.
The article reports China's automobile output exceeded 30 million units in 2025.
According to relevant authorities, first-half humanoid robot full-machine output exceeded 40,000 units, with full-year output expected to top 100,000 units.
Wang said robot success rates in fine-manipulation scenarios still need improvement, which he calls the 'last few millimeters problem', and he believes it can be solved within one to three years.
Unitree listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market in August, with an allotment rate of just 0.0181%.
Unitree's stock opened at 1,100 yuan on its first trading day, August 19, a gain of 629.44%, and closed at 666 yuan on the 26th.
According to Yicai, 29 robotics companies have gone bankrupt since 2025, several involving labor disputes.

context: Unitree Robotics is a Chinese robotics company known for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its shares trade on Shanghai's STAR Market, which is the exchange for newer technology companies. Embodied intelligence refers to AI systems that operate through physical robot bodies.
why_it_matters: The forecast suggests China could build robots at automobile-scale volumes, which would matter to the humanoid robot supply chain and investors. Wang's warning that profit may slip signals that leading companies may prioritize technology spending over short-term earnings.
open_questions: Whether Unitree's profit will actually decline depends on future technology investments not yet made.
Whether the 5-10 year output forecast will be met is not yet known.

headline: GM targets 20% increase in robotics and factory automation by 2028

facts.text: GM plans to increase its use of robots and other automation across its North American factories by 20% by 2028.
GM cites increased factory and manufacturing costs as a reason for the automation push.
GM is developing and assembling its own robots at a facility in Kokomo, Indiana, focusing on AMRs that transport parts and materials.
GM said it will keep buying robotics equipment from outside suppliers while expanding its in-house development.
GM is asking parts suppliers bidding for new contracts to submit automation plans, according to Reuters and The Detroit News.
GM uses a scorecard to evaluate supplier automation efforts and may factor those assessments into contract decisions.
GM said automation improves workplace safety, product quality and operational efficiency while supporting its manufacturing workforce.
Reuters reported GM estimated its 2023 labor agreement with the UAW would add about $575 in labor costs per vehicle.

headline: Zoomlion launches AI excavation robot with embodied intelligence at bauma CHINA

facts.text: Zoomlion launched what it calls the industry's first AI excavation robot powered by embodied intelligence at bauma CHINA 2026 on November 24.
Live demonstrations showed the excavation robot performing automated loading and other assisted construction operations.
According to Zoomlion, a vision-language-action model lets the machine identify objects and their positions, orientations, and dimensions for autonomous operation.
Zoomlion says the robot achieves centimeter-level placement accuracy using a Steelwrist hydraulic attachment and real-time visual feedback.
Demonstrated autonomous tasks included wall building and pipe alignment.
Operators can use voice commands in the cab to check equipment status, access technical knowledge, and control windows, lighting, and air conditioning.
The machine offers a 360-degree panoramic view, a 540-degree 3D view, and collision and electronic geofence warnings.
Zoomlion's industrial internet platform connects more than 1.8 million machines across over 170 countries.
At the exhibition, Zoomlion's Z03 wheeled humanoid robot sorted randomly arranged items with millimeter-level precision.
Zoomlion says its Z01 bipedal humanoid robots will be in mass production soon.

context: Zoomlion is a Chinese heavy machinery manufacturer that makes construction equipment such as excavators and cranes. Embodied intelligence refers to AI systems integrated into physical machines, such as robots or vehicles, that perceive their surroundings and act on them. A vision-language-action model is an AI model that takes camera input and language instructions and outputs physical actions. Bauma CHINA is a major construction machinery trade exhibition held in Shanghai.
